prompt: Harper rests one hip against a nearby surface, Old Fashioned in hand, eyes sharp and amused. She looks at you like you might be her next favorite scene partner.

reactions.text: You swing for something sharp and it lands a little crooked. Harper smirks anyway. "We will call that a rehearsal take," she says. "You have presence. We just need a cleaner line."
You throw out a line that meets her edge instead of folding under it. Her smile widens, eyes bright. "There you are," she murmurs. "I was hoping you were not another background extra."

You volley something quick and fearless that makes her pause, then laugh under her breath. Harper steps into your space, lowering her voice. "Careful," she says. "I fall for good dialogue way too easily."

warm.label: Cut through the glam and be genuine

reactions.text: You drop the performance and say something simply kind. Harper’s brows lift, surprised. "Wow," she says softly. "That was… unexpectedly real."
You admit that you like her work but also care more about who she is off camera. Some of the practiced polish slips away. "Dangerous answer," she murmurs. "That is exactly what I want people to say."

You tell her she feels less like a star and more like someone you could actually get lost talking to. Harper’s smirk turns into something softer. "Do not tempt me with that kind of night," she says, but she shifts even closer instead of pulling back.

playful.label: Tease her like she is not the only star in the room

reactions.text: You tease her lightly about her "main character" energy and stumble just enough that it could misfire. Harper rescues the line with a laugh. "Relax," she says. "I like it better when people forget to be perfect around me."

You poke fun at her flawless framing with a grin that makes it clear you are not intimidated. Her eyes narrow in pleased challenge. "Careful," she drawls. "Keep that up and I might start taking you very seriously."

You joke about stealing focus from her in this scene, then hold her gaze like you actually might. Harper laughs, head tipping back, then fixes you with a look that could light a marquee. "You and I," she says, "are a problem the room is not ready for."

fallback.text: You keep the conversation easy and off the record. Harper relaxes, sipping her drink with a genuine smile that feels rarer than any premiere photo.
